subject: Nanotechnology
title: Nanoparticles in Water Systems
description: One-minute skill: Nanoparticles in Water Systems.

hook.text: Nano silver washed from your socks enters the sewer — what happens when it reaches the river?

buildup.text: Wastewater treatment captures most nanoparticles in sludge — but a fraction passes through into surface water.

discovery.text: In the environment, silver nanoparticles transform into silver sulfide — less toxic but persistent in sediment.

twist.text: Sludge containing nanoparticles is often spread on farmland as fertilizer — returning them to the food chain.

climax.text: Long-term studies track nano accumulation in soil organisms — earthworms and microbes are early warning indicators.

punchline.text: Nano goes down the drain and comes back through the soil — a silent loop.

quiz.question: How do nanoparticles from consumer products re-enter the food chain?
options: They evaporate from wastewater into the atmosphere
Sewage sludge containing captured nanoparticles is spread on farmland as fertilizer
Fish absorb them directly from tap water
